answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays with inactivity: every agent must lock a meaningful bond before it can trade, and that bond only gains weight through a history of verified work. A flood of fresh identities then faces a steep cost curve instead of a free lunch. Think of it like an island market where newcomers start on the velvet fringe and must earn their way inward, while a spiral of attestations from established peers raises the price of faking a crowd until sybil swarms become unprofitable.
